VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9, 2025
  2525 GRAND AVENUE, LONG BEACH, 90815
  , 5:00 PM

Kenneth Osborn, Chair  James Goodin, Commissioner
Antawnette Atkins Blade, Vice Chair  James Schotter, Commissioner
Juanita Doplemore, Commissioner  Nicholas Sramek, Commissioner

  FINISHED AGENDA & MINUTES

CALL TO ORDER

Vice Chair Atkins Blade called the meeting to order at 5 p.m.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present: Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter

Also present: Gina Overholt, Coordinator.

Also in attendance: Ryan Antes, Shawn Jones, Steve Hageman, and John Donnigan.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

Commissioner Schotter led the Pledge of Allegiance.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  25-54962  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Veterans Affairs Commission
  meeting of Wednesday, February 12, 2025.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Doplemore, seconded by
  Commissioner Schotter, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by
  the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

2.  25-54963  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on a Veterans and Service
  Members Job Fair on April 17.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Doplemore, seconded by

  Commissioner Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by
  the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

  Staff shared the details on the upcoming Veteran and Service Member Job Fair, a
  collaboration between Health (Office of Veterans Support) and Economic
  Development (Workforce Innovation Network), led by Health Department Public
  Service Fellow Alexandria O’ Board. Commissioners were invited to attend and to
  promote the event to their contacts. The Job Fair includes 20 employers, six service
  providers (e.g. housing assistance, mental health, health care), and three
  workshops: an LBPD recruitment and Q & A, financial education and navigating the
  VA home loan process. It also includes a resume bar, lunch, while supplies last,
  professional head shots and more. Commissioners were invited to attend the event
  as well as volunteer.

3.  25-54964  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Veterans Banner
  Program.

  Chair of the Veterans Banner subcommittee and staff liaison reported on project
  progress. Nearly 150 nominations were received, the breakdown of nominees by
  service branch, race, ethnicity and other demographics were shared. The
  subcommittee selected three locations for the banners, Long Beach
  Airport/Lakewood Blvd. (between Conant and Spring St.), VA Long Beach (between
  Bellflower Blvd. & 7th St.) and St. Mary’s Hospital (Atlantic Ave. between 8th &
  11th). The Commission approved the proposed banner locations.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Osborn, seconded by Commissioner
  Sramek, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

4.  25-54965  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation from the Community Crisis

  Response Team.

  Community Crisis Response Program Manager Anthony Montalvo presented on the
  Community Crisis Response Team, which provides an alternative (non-law
  enforcement) emergency response to eligible non-violent 911calls-for-service with a
  focus on behavioral health and quality of life issues. Approximately five percent of
  the nearly 600 clients responded to by the CCR team (through December 2024)
  were Veterans. Commissioners are invited to attend the event as well as volunteer.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Sramek, seconded by Commissioner
  Goodin, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

5.  25-54966  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on USS Frank E. Evans and the
  Lost 74 commemoration on June 3.

  Staff reported on ongoing planning for this event, a collaboration between USS
  Frank E. Evans Association and the Office of Veterans Support to commemorate
  the Evans and the upcoming renaming of the 710/PCH junction and adjacent bridge
  for USS Frank E. Evans Lost 74, celebrate our city’s naval history, and observe
  Memorial Day. The Port of Long Beach is lead sponsor. The media release draft is
  moving through the City approvals process. Commissioners are invited to attend
  the event as well as serve as volunteers, helping with event promotion, set-up,
  clean-up and staffing the OVS information booth.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Osborn, seconded by Commissioner
  Doplemore, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

6.  25-54967  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on changes to Chapter 2.60 of
  the Long Beach Municipal Code related to the Veterans Affairs Commission.

  Page 3 of 5
   VETERANS AFFAIRS COMMISSION MINUTES
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 9, 2025
  2525 GRAND AVENUE, LONG BEACH, 90815
  , 5:00 PM

  Ensuring quorum for Commission meetings is increasingly challenging.
  Commissioners who stepped down in June because they had already served four
  consecutive terms have not been easily replaced because of the one Commissioner
  per Council district requirement. Accordingly, a motion was initially made to
  consider reducing the number of Commissioners to seven and to relinquish the
  requirement that there be one Commissioner per Council district but instead
  stipulate that there be no more than two Commissioners from a single district on the
  Commission. Because so much of the Commission’s work is carried out by
  subcommittees and we just learned that these subcommittees may only be
  composed of members of the Commission, a revised motion was proposed to keep
  the number of Commissioners at nine and stipulate that there be no more than two
  Commissioners from a single Council district.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Osborn, seconded by Commissioner
  Doplemore, to approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following
  vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

7.  25-54968  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on a recommendation to Council
  in support of keeping Long Beach Veterans Administration funding and jobs intact.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Atkins Blade, seconded by
  Commissioner Doplemore, to approve recommendation. The
  motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Goodin, Osborn, Doplemore, Sramek, Atkins Blade, Schotter
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 0  None

  Commission discussed creating a letter of support or a resolution wherein the
  Commission would make a statement in support of the LB VA that Council would
  approve and submit to the federal government.

consideration in May.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Staff shared information on the US VETS 5K event on May 25. Future agenda items: same subjects

Chair Osborn adjourned meeting at 6:46 p.m.
